messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple EVPN adjacency flaps observed across eu-west3 edge POPs, starting 1954320995. Symptoms: increased p95/p99 latency, rising 502/503 errors for hosted API endpoints routed via eu-west3, and queueing on several Dedicated pools. Monitoring: https://metrics.redwood/evpn/eu-west3 (graphs)

oncall-net: Ack. Paging @sre-kate and @infra-jin. I see BGP session resets to two eBGP neighbors (LAX peering and AMS transit). Possible upstream maintenance or flapping link.

sre-kate: On it. Quick impact check: which customer traffic is egressing via those POPs? Also confirm whether this is dataplane-only (EGRESS) or internal fabric.

cs-mike: Quick list: Dedicated customers ACorp, StudioHQ, Finlytics have reserved pools in eu-west3. Self-serve API shows elevated 502s across small/medium tenants using eu-west3 region. Seeing increased ticket volume.

infra-jin: Confirmed eBGP adjacency resets on routers eu-west3-rtr-1 and -3, likely due to upstream route flap. I can push temporary more-specific announcements to steer traffic via eu-central1 peers and relax BGP timers for affected routers. Will do rolling change now.

eng-runtime: Note: several model serving queues in eu-west3 hit >70% concurrency and started shedding requests per SLO policy. We have failover paths: smart-router can route to eu-central1 model replicas. We need to coordinate swap to avoid mass cold-starts.

sre-kate: Plan: 1) immediate mitigation: infra-jin to announce steering routes -> eu-central1; 2) eng-runtime to enable smart-router fallback to eu-central1 for affected hostnames (soft failover + preserve sticky sessions for Dedicated if possible); 3) status page + customer comms. Who can draft the public status?

product-ops: I'll draft. Need clear language on impact and ETA for resolution. Also note affected customers (by region) for account teams.

infra-jin: Done: announced /24s to prefer eu-central1 transit at 1954321165. BGP hold-time bumped to 6s on eu-west3-rtr-1/3 at 1954321180. Route filters updated to avoid re-advertising problematic prefixes. Early telemetry: egress success rate improved for some flows, but latency +120-160ms for steered flows.

eng-runtime: Rolled soft-failover for non-Dedicated hostnames at 1954321280 (gradual weight shift 80/20). Dedicated pools are sticky; we'll need explicit approval to migrate reserved capacity. Queueing reduced from 70% -> 35% for routes shifted.

sre-kate: Drafting status page copy, please review:```
Status: Degraded
Components: Edge network (EU - eu-west3)
Impact: Some customers may experience increased latency and intermittent 502/503 errors when routing through eu-west3. Certain Dedicated customers in eu-west3 may see degraded throughput.
Mitigation: We are steering traffic to eu-central1 peers and enabling smart-router fallback while we work with transit providers to stabilize EVPN sessions. Temporary latency increase expected for affected traffic.
ETA: Monitoring for stabilization; no ETA yet for full BGP flap resolution. We will provide updates every 30 minutes.
```

product-ops: That's clear. Recommend adding a line for account teams to reach out: "Account teams will follow up with Dedicated customers with tailored mitigation (capacity migration, credits)."

cs-mike: Approving the customer-facing wording. Also sharing a quick customer notification template for account teams to use:```
Hi <CustomerName>,
We're experiencing degraded connectivity for traffic routed through eu-west3 due to an edge network routing flap. We've temporarily steered your traffic to eu-central1 which may increase latency by ~120ms. Our engineering team is working with upstream providers to restore normal routing. If you'd like us to migrate your Dedicated capacity to eu-central1 temporarily, reply and we'll prioritize.
Apologies for the disruption — we'll update you within 30 minutes or on major status changes.
Thanks, Redwood CS
```

sre-kate: Good. Product-ops, please post the public status: set as "Degraded" and include per-region notes (eu-west3 impacted, eu-central1 receiving failover traffic but serving, eu-west1 unaffected). Also post to internal #eng-ops with runbook link.

product-ops: Posted public status at 1954321450 and pinged #eng-ops with the runbook. Also created a private note for account teams with the customer template and list of affected Dedicated customers.

incident-bot: UPDATE: Incident severity set to SEV2. Pager still active. Next automated update scheduled in 30 minutes.

oncall-net: Handing off active monitoring to eng-runtime for follow-up on traffic steering, preserving logs for postmortem. @eng-runtime take it from here; I'll remain available for routing changes. Last check: bgp resets frequency down from 12/min -> 2/min.

eng-runtime: Ack. I'll monitor request success rates and coordinate with infra-jin for any additional route adjustments. Will send a follow-up summary in 15-20 minutes with per-customer impact and any required action items for Dedicated migrations.

cs-mike: Thanks. I'm standing by to notify accounts if we start migrations.

sre-kate: Good work. Keep updates coming. We'll keep this thread as the main comms channel for the incident.

oncall-net: Logging handoff at 1954322367. Monitoring only.
